summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with HCV- and alcohol-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma s/p TACE and recent RFA, and chronic depression presented with diffuse abdominal pain and nausea. She reported poor pain control despite IV hydromorphone and requested trazodone and zolpidem. Evaluation revealed no acute surgical or infectious cause; labs were stable, ultrasound showed a cirrhotic liver without ascites or focal lesion, and KUB demonstrated stool-filled colon. Pain was attributed to constipation, and lactulose was increased. She declined narcotics and sedatives due to liver disease risks. By morning, she reported improvement and readiness for discharge. She was discharged home with continued home medications, ondansetron for nausea, and follow-up plans with her liver and primary care teams. Social work was involved due to significant psychosocial stressors.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of liver
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
